Abilities: Echo Spirit is her first charlatan ability; Bait and Switch, Rune Trap, Force Tether, Lightning Tether and Pit of the Reaper; shapeshifting. Storage: a personal storage space that even the Magic Society cannot peek into "without killing her first". Familiars: Shimmer, a summoned astral lantern, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.
97.name: Belinda Callahan

98.content: Beth Cavendish is a bronze-rank Greenstone adventurer and water healer who leads a team in the Ustei campaign and the City of Fallen Echoes. Competent and brisk, she gives orders without ceremony. Brisk: "We're going to move on the sand barge". Encouraging: "Welcome to the path to bronze rank". Compared with Cassandra's brother: Cassandra says the way Jason describes his brother reminds her of Beth. Water healer; Jason envies her affliction-blanketing powers. Struck down by the thorn fountain's retributive damage in the Fallen Echoes fight. Introduces herself to Jason at the Adventure Society as Beth Cavendish, meeting her cousin Mose. The Cavendish family names a Greenstone district. Hudson, Niko, Emily, Mose: team members.
98.name: Beth Cavendish

99.content: Clarissa Ventress is one of the crime lords of Old City and holds Sophie's indenture. She uses Sophie to provoke the rash Cole Silva and learns what Lucian Lamprey wants in order to control him. Calculating: "The key to controlling a person was finding what they wanted". Amused: she is "happily imagining the look on Silva's face" as she watches Sophie's match. Irritated by independence: she is less happy with Sophie's friend Belinda. Rank is not stated in the lines read; she travels with a huge leonid bodyguard. Lives in a sprawling manor in Old City's canal district, which has its own internal city wall. Her arrangement with Sophie: Sophie would help her provoke Silva into the kind of rash action his father would have prevented. Sophie: indentured servant. Cole Silva: rival, newest of the Big Three. Lucian Lamprey: someone she plans to control.
99.name: Clarissa Ventress

100.content: Clive Standish is a tall, lanky Magic Society researcher in Greenstone, raised on an eel farm, who becomes Jason's team's ritualist and astral-magic scholar. He explains the cosmos to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup, identifies the Reaper-trial astral space as a Builder vessel, and builds the open-access Magical Research Association. A lecturer who loses the thread and apologises; he wants dumpling soup in the middle of his own lecture on the cosmos. He says he venerates, not worships, the Celestial Book: "There's a difference"; an archbishop asks "You admit to being a heretic?" and Clive answers that he "could be considered a heretic". He jokes about his background: "I'm the son of eel farmers". A stranger accuses him of sleeping with a wife he says he does not have, which becomes a running gag. Essences: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. A rune essence came to him as "an epic four-star essence". Abilities: Wrath of the Magister, a rune circle that triggers effects when attacked, the damage-reflecting buff Mantle of Retribution and the zone ability Eye of Karma; Mana Equilibrium. Racial gift: a blessing from the Celestial Book changed his human Special Attack Affinity into a spell affinity. Familiar: Onslow, a rune tortoise who sits at the prow of the airboat, carries Clive, and becomes a runic tattoo on his torso when called back. Ritual and astral magic: he leads the team's rituals and bridge research.
100.name: Clive Standish

101.content: Cressida Vane is the matriarch of the blood-cult family that holds Jason and his friends in Book 1. Beautiful, haughty and weary of her family's ambitions, she insists they are "a nice, traditional blood cult family" and she is killed in the confrontation. Haughty: "I am Lady Cressida Vane"; Jason mocks her high-priestess name. Traditional: "This is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way". Dismissive of her husband: "I don't care what my stupid husband thinks; he married into the family". Leader of the blood cult family's rituals. Complained that astral beings were "the death" of her son. Mother of Landemere Vane; she asks what Landemere was trying to summon. Darryl: the high priest beside her.
101.name: Cressida Vane

102.content: Danielle Geller is Humphrey's mother and the head of the Geller family's household in Greenstone. She is a silver-ranker at the start of the series who looks much younger than she is, later a gold-ranker with dimension and time powers, and Jason's political adviser on Earth. Time: a time confluence, with only forward time travel possible; in Book 3 she outpaces Lucian Lamprey in a fight, teleporting behind him and cutting his neck. She is called "Time Witch of Vitesse". Dimension: a dimension essence, as Emir says, with gold rank from the notes; she teleports behind Lamprey in a fight. Estate and training: the Geller estate's mirage chamber can run at bronze rank only "for limited periods" because Greenstone's magic is low, and at iron rank Danielle offers it to Rufus; a family member from the generation that first settled the region may still be alive. The diamond-rank ancestor in the earlier notes was not found.
102.name: Danielle Geller

103.content: An ice-armoured defender from the Kettering family who starts as one of Thadwick Mercer's offsiders, joins Rick's team in Book 2 and later fights beside Neil in Cardinas. One of Thadwick Mercer's two offsiders with Neil: he protects the group with his powers while Neil heals them. The Davone and Kettering families have close ties to the Mercers, which is how the boys came to Thadwick's side. He and Neil are relieved to be free, having been known as Thadwick's flunkeys. A local who fills Jonah Geller's defender role on Rick's team: "a classic defender, not very mobile but very hard to go around or through", clad in armour forged entirely of ice. His cousin Hudson Kettering is his counterpart on Beth Cavendish's team.
103.name: Dustin Kettering

key: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
104.comment: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
104.content: A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning. Jason has three, each very different, and Humphrey has one.
keys: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
104.name: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash

105.content: Farrah Hurin (also spelt Huren) is a small, pale, strawberry-blonde ritual magician from Vitesse. She is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, teaches him aura control, perception and meditation, and treats him as an equal. Essences: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence; she explains this herself in Book 1. Abilities: lava cannon, a magma golem, lava streams and fire orbs, obsidian domes, shards and columns, and obsidian armour. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and builds the infrastructure of Asano Village and the Grid repairs. Aura teaching: perception and memory games, meditation and aura control.
105.name: Farrah Hurin

106.content: Gareth "Gary" Xandier is an enormous leonid smith and warrior from Vitesse. He makes Jason's first sword, Dread Salvation. Summon: a foundry golem, a roughly three-metre black-iron figure with a molten mouth that drips molten metal. Equipment: conjured full-body dark-steel plate armour; the notes add a hammer and shield and the runes. Smithing: he forges Dread Salvation; he reforges it with his mentor Virid Martine as Hegemon's Will. Rank: bronze at the start; "almost silver" by Book 3; silver after using a core. Demigod: Hero's power makes him a demigod, "a vision of physical might, wreathed in divine power".
106.name: Gary (Gareth Xandier) and Gary Sharpton

107.content: Twin elf sisters on Rick Geller's team: Hannah the archer and Claire the healer. The elf twins Hannah and Claire Adeah are the archer and the team healer, with Claire the most important member to protect. Hannah's arrows pin trap weavers to trees; Claire cleanses afflictions and cuts a team mate from a web with her wand. In the Book 1 mock battle against Jason, Claire's body is left floating in the water after she focused her healing on the others, and they swear revenge. Claire resented Jason's tactics in the mock battle the most.
107.name: Hannah and Claire Adeah

108.content: Hudson Kettering is the huge earth-essence front-liner of Beth Cavendish's team and cousin of Dustin Kettering. He is a stone-shielding bruiser who meets Jason on the sand barge assault, fights Humphrey in a Geller-versus-Cavendish contest, and joins the Reaper trial expedition. Size: "One of the members of Beth's team was a huge human named Hudson. He looked like Humphrey with twenty percent bonus person, to the point of being almost as large as Gary". First meeting: he tells Jason "You don't seem evil". Team role: Beth puts him "front and centre" in the assault on the sand barge, and a large flat block of sandstone rises under the team to carry them forward like a raft. In the fight: a bronze-rank captain's charge shatters his stone shield and sends him staggering; he ploughs up the ramp "crashing into the people inside and making space for the others". Beth tells him "No slacking". Family: he is cousin to Dustin, "the only one I can think of who could stack up to Jonah" among defenders, and cannot be pried from Beth's team. Dustin sits beside him with their teams around them. Humphrey's offer: Jason brings Humphrey to talk to Hudson about his cousin joining a Geller team; Hudson says a Geller name is good "but so was Mercer", and the family wants real adventurers for Dustin after Thadwick. Memorial: his team attends the memorial because "Her standing strong is the reason my team all got out alive".
108.name: Hudson Kettering

109.content: Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller is the leader of Team Biscuit, a tall, broad-shouldered, handsome young man from a family that has been adventuring for sixteen generations. He begins the series a shy teenager and becomes a steady leader and one of the team's strongest fighters. Formal in a crisis: in Book 3, facing the Builder's forces, he announces "My name is Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller. My family have been adventurers for sixteen generations. We aren't alchemists or weaponsmiths on the side... For hundreds of years we have done one thing, and one thing only: protect our world from people like you". Shy in personal matters: when Jason asks in front of his mother whether he has spoken to Gabrielle, he turns white and shakes his head. Moral voice: in Book 1 he confronts Jason about the cruelty of the mirage-arena ambush. He later advises against elaborate plans: "We tried that fifteen years ago and we only got from Rimaros to Yaresh". Essences: the dragon confluence, reached through the might and wing essences. Abilities include dragon wings and a flaming dragon-wing sword, a Dragon's Might aura that turns fire into dragon fire, teleporting, and the ability Spartoi, which at gold rank calls up a hundred dragon-tooth bone-golem warriors in blue and gold armour. Racial gift: his human gift Special Attack Affinity evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon and later into Hero's Drive, with the racial gift Hero's Sacrifice.
109.name: Humphrey Geller

110.content: Jason Asano is the series' protagonist: an Australian from the coastal town of Casselton Beach who, at twenty-three, is pulled across the cosmos to Pallimustus by a failed summoning. Humour and references: he jokes constantly and quotes films and television. He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart"; he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine. He says "G'day" and "mate". Self-deprecation: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities". He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway". Essences: Dark, Blood, Sin and the Doom confluence. His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence). Way of the Reaper martial arts. The set Regalia of the Dark Hegemon includes the Amulet of the Dark Guardian. Abilities seen in the text: Path of Shadows, Midnight Eyes, Castigate and Verdict, Punition, Feast of Absolution and Gordon's Harbinger of Doom. Outworlder racial abilities: Interface, Quest System, Inventory, Map, Astral Affinity and Mysterious Stranger. Mysterious Stranger gives language adaptation, absorption of essences, awakening stones and skill books, and immunity to identification and tracking effects. Astral Affinity increases resistance to dimension effects and astral forces and increases the effect of dimension abilities and transcendent damage.
110.name: Jason Asano

111.content: Knowledge is the goddess of Knowledge. Jason meets her in Book 1 on arriving at her temple, and for twelve books she charms and manipulates him.
111.name: Knowledge

112.content: Neil Davone is an elf of Greenstone's Island families, a healer who grows from the Mercers' hanger-on into the heart of Jason's team. He is a priest of the Healer, and by 2038 he uses his growth magic to reclaim deserts. Essences: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence: short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing. Abilities: size-growth power and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time; the Reaper's Redoubt. Summon: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit. Late: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa.
112.name: Neil Davone

113.content: Nicolas Hendren is the archbishop of the Church of Purity, a silver-rank barrier-and-force specialist who flees the inquiry and joins the Builder cult's camp before Jason's team kills him. Stiff, proud and rule-bound, he wants Purity's dignity even as it is dragged into the cult's plans. Disgruntled and proud: he is summoned to the cult camp and refuses to taint the church for "short-term power". Moral authority absent god: his god's voice is silent, making him the highest moral authority in the realm he stands in. Silver-rank barrier and force specialist: his barrier shields his group from a falling building; a force wave power; "always the true danger". Archbishop of the Church of Purity, introduced at a Greenstone meeting. One Book 3 line spells the name Hedron. The Builder cult: reluctant ally.
113.name: Nicolas Hendren

114.content: Padma Parsell is an adventurer from Remore Academy and Farrah's half-disciple, who leads a Vitesse team in the City of Fallen Echoes. Keen, grieving and quick to speak her mind, she treats Jason as a rival after Farrah's death. Keen and grieving: Farrah was her idol and mentor; she lets Jason vent her frustration. Obedient to instructors: Instructor Gabriel's voice triggers conditioned obedience. Ignores interruptions: when Lance calls out under his breath, she ignores him. Leader of a Vitesse team of Rufus's juniors. Trained at Remore Academy a few years behind Rufus. She had waited for Farrah's return to Vitesse and, when Farrah died, joined Emir's call for adventurers.
114.name: Padma Parsell

115.content: Rufus Remore is a bald, dark-skinned swordsman from Vitesse, grandson of the diamond-ranker Roland Remore. He is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, runs Jason's field assessment, and remains his friend for the rest of the series. He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say. He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous. After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships. Swordsmanship: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand; silver and golden swords. Other powers: boots that let him walk on water and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time". Kingdom of Eclipse: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation. Teaching: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat and later teaches the Asano clan.
115.name: Rufus Remore

116.content: Sophie Wexler is a celestine fighter known as the Nightingale in the Greenstone fighting pits. She is a thief and debt-slave when Jason meets her, has her indenture taken over by Jason in Book 2, and becomes the team's fastest fighter and, later, Humphrey's fiancée. Essences: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years. Abilities: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades; Between the Raindrops; Mirage Step and Wind Blade; unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes. Racial gifts (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring, Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity, and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament.
116.name: Sophie Wexler

117.content: Timos is a Builder cultist embedded in Greenstone for years who regrets going along with Thadwick's self-recruitment, kills Frank, and stands with Zato in the Vane estate ritual. He is careful, patient and horrified by amateurs. Regretful: he "quickly came to regret" Thadwick's aggressive self-recruitment. Cautious: every mistake "threatened to snowball into disaster". Compartmentalising: he facilitated the cult's insertions and ran operatives in compartmentalised groups. He kills Frank with a conjured spear. He takes part in a ritual with Zato and Dougall. "Timos had been operating in Greenstone for years". Thadwick: an inconvenient recruit.
117.name: Timos

118.content: A swordmaster prince of the Kingdom of Mirrors whom Clive meets in the City of Fallen Echoes; he is cheerful, reckless and a rival and friend to Jason's team. Introduces himself as "Valdis" and praises Clive's reputation; the system names him Valdis Volaire. A prince of the small but influential Kingdom of Mirrors, whose borders have not changed in eight centuries; his father, the Mirror King, is eight hundred years old and the kingdom is "thick with princes and princesses". A reckless enthusiast who leads his three teammates up a tower in search of treasure; he has a light-step power, a slow-fall power and a wall run. He chooses the path of courage in the trial and is the first to step forward. A sword master, mobile striker and the stronger team's leader; his team is a highly efficient cohort trained since before they had essences. His father collects him from Jason's ship, to Valdis's embarrassment; he portals in for Jason's memorial.
118.name: Valdis Volaire

119.content: Zara is a celestine princess of the Storm Kingdom, the "Hurricane Princess". Jason meets her in a tent during the contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, when she is nineteen and he is iron-rank. Years later the scandal of her false engagement claim, her loss of the succession, and her adoption into her mother's house bring her to Team Biscuit and, in 2038, into a romance with Jason. Powers: wind and water, big storms; recovery, speed, astral and holy affinity.
119.name: Zara Rimaros (Zara Nareen)

120.content: Zato is the silver-rank leader of the Builder cult's local forces in Book 3, a metal-bodied shapeshifter who recruits Thadwick, drives the cult's survivors to the Vane Estate and is the final opponent of Jason's team. He is competent, unfazed and sure of victory. On top of things: Jason says "He does seem pretty on top of things... I actually kind of like him" and invites him to join team "Hopelessly Outmatched". Convinced of victory: "Zato knew that his victory was imminent. He knew that the adventurers were no match for his power". Quiet in command: he stands with his back to the door, eyes lingering on Timos's neck marks, saying nothing. Recruiter: "I see your true potential". Silver rank, with a metal body of shifting abilities. Immovable in the final fight: no damage seems to impair him, even Humphrey's strikes. Trump card: after baiting out Sophie's absorb power, his body explodes into a mass of shrapnel. "The last silver-ranker left in the Builder cult's local forces"; tasked with leading the evacuation when the island stronghold was invaded, he escaped with a good number of people, though none of the other silver-rankers survived. Thadwick Mercer: his recruit. Humphrey and Sophie: opponents in the climax. Timos: his follower, whose neck he notices.
120.name: Zato

121.content: Jason's first familiar: a swarm of apocalypse leeches that lives in his blood, sprays out over enemies to bite and drain them, and can take the shape of a red-eyed blood clone of Jason. Colin begins as a hungry, wriggling swarm and grows into a being who talks back, waves from his bowl of leeches and calls Jason "smarmy". Named: Jason says, "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin", and calls the swarm "Leechy" in the same fight. Lives in Jason's blood: Jason pricks his finger and the leeches crawl into his hand and vanish into his blood. His rapid regeneration only works while the familiar is in his bloodstream. Method: Jason sprays him out over a target like a fire hose and Colin crawls over armour to find flesh. Colin wiggles happily when pleased. Where he comes from: a summoned familiar is created through different means from the sanguine horror, but Clive observes it is what Jason summoned, and if Jason reached diamond his familiar would reach the full strength of a sanguine horror.
121.name: Colin

122.content: Jason's third familiar: an Avatar of Doom, a floating cloak holding a nebula in the shape of an eye, circled by blue and orange eye-orbs that fire beams. He cannot speak, but he answers questions with his orbs and has a distinct personality, and he is the key to the intrinsic-mandate magic Jason uses to work with authority. Summoned: the doom essence ability Avatar of Doom summons a familiar. At first it is unnamed, an iron-rank incorporeal familiar whose orbs make sustained beams, one of disruptive force and one of resonating force, and whose damage leaves Vulnerable. Named: asked if it wants a name, it flashes its blue orb, and Jason says, "I'm going to call you... Gordon". Orange is no and blue is yes: Gordon's orange orb flashes brightly as his signal for no. Shade relays him: "Gordon says that I should be last". Appearance: a disembodied cloak with a nebula-like cloud of blue and orange in the shape of an eye, and eyeball-patterned orbs drifting around it that fire unrelenting beams. In a fight: his beams inflict Vulnerable on a lizard; his energy dash is fast but his reflexes are sluggish, and a blow can dissipate his vessel entirely.
122.name: Gordon

123.content: Clive Standish's familiar: a rune tortoise whose shell carries runes that throw elemental attacks, and whose shell the whole team rides in, shelters in and runs the battlefield from. Onslow is gentle and a little stubborn, and Clive talks to him as "little buddy". First sight: Onslow is at the front of Clive's airboat with his head jutting forward "like a dog with its head out a car window". Clive sits on his shell with Jason beside him. Powers: he fires elemental attacks from the magic runes on his shell, which Clive recharges with his own mana. A rune dims when he takes a hit. A seat for the team: Clive picks up Stash and climbs on Onslow's shell with Neil, and the tortoise floats off the rooftop on a cushion of air. Clive drops down off him when the tower is threatened.
123.name: Onslow

124.content: Jason's shadow familiar, a formal, dry astral being who is one of the Reaper's shadows. He first appears as the keeper of the Reaper trials, becomes Jason's closest and most constant companion, and acts as his butler, driver, spy and sounding board. He says himself that he is a shepherd of death, and that he has changed more than the others of his kind. The invigilator: he appears as the shadowy figure who runs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes and offers to explain their practical dangers or their origins. He hands out vials and medallions with his shadowy hands, which are cold to the touch. A familiar before: he tells the competitors that the grandmaster who built the place was an outworlder with the dark essence like Jason, "I was his summoned familiar once". Summoned by Jason: when Jason chooses to summon a familiar after the trials, he greets Shade with "I was hoping it would be you". Bodies: he appears as three bodies that become horses for a ride or large lizards for rough terrain, and his bodies move among monsters as elusive shadowy figures. The Reaper's child: the Reaper says "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path".
124.name: Shade

125.content: Belinda Callahan's astral lantern: a small living lantern that orbits her, projects shields, fires force bolts and feeds mana to her team. It is the quietest of the team's familiars, but it is on the field in almost every battle. Summoned: the final ability of Belinda's power set is a summoned familiar, an astral lantern. Belinda names it: "How about Shimmer?". In a fight: it projects shields to protect the team and, with Gordon, beams the enemy to split their attention. The force bolts of a lantern familiar prove more dangerous to its own side against Hendren's defences.
125.name: Shimmer

126.content: Humphrey Geller's bonded familiar: a baby mirage dragon whose full name is Velitraxistaasch, who prefers "Stash". He changes shape constantly, starts as a barking lizard, a bird or a puppy and ends up large enough to crush a company of messengers, and he talks, mostly in cheerful, blunt remarks. Name: "It's short for Velitraxistaasch. He likes 'Stash,' though.". Jason works out what he is at once and Humphrey is startled. Bond: "Our mothers arranged him becoming my familiar. Or me becoming his person, depending on how you look at it". A bonded familiar is an actual magical creature that can die, unlike a summoned familiar. Shapes: a canary on Humphrey's head and a puppy, a bird that swoops from the sky and turns into a puppy in his arms, a barking lizard, and a bark lurker or a darting bird in a fight. Biscuits: Jason feeds him a biscuit and he turns into a puppy to snuffle it from Jason's hand, then yaps his agreement. Speech: "Stash chase worm! Stash chase worm!". Scouting: he leads Humphrey's party by barking in the right direction to the margolls. Special attack: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
126.name: Stash

127.content: For about a year after the Reaper trials, a hidden cult of the Builder works inside Greenstone's aristocracy and through the church of Purity. It implants star seeds, suborns Thadwick Mercer and others, and prepares to claim an astral space. Jason's team learns of it in Book 2 and breaks it in Book 3, ending in the astral space the cult built and the death of Jason.

128.content: After Farrah's death, Emir Bahadir opens an astral space in the delta and invites iron-rank teams to compete for the legacy of the Order of the Reaper. The City of Fallen Echoes holds the trials, a shipful of time-displaced priests and a Reaper-run test of virtue. Jason's team wins a set of rewards, and the tale of the Order's survival becomes a live question. Launch: iron-rankers board the cloud ship once the palace has resumed its shape; adventurers spread across Sky Scar Lake by every means. The zone is "City of Fallen Echoes (Gate Tower Three)". Shade's account: the legacy goes to whoever embodies the ideals of the Order; the last grandmaster sent all the initiates into the city; the vorger do not kill, and the initiates were turned into abominations. The city: siege golems and flesh abominations adapt to how they are fought. Imran Keane joins Jason's party. A blood root vine is hit with Inexorable Doom. Rival teams: Padma's team is the last to join, and Beth's team stays put beside Jason's near the end. Before the trials Beth's and Rick's teams had met in the mirage chamber contest. All reach the city centre, where Humphrey's team staggers in ragged. The final day: Shade announces that the second trial ends in one day and warns of nightmare hags, diamond-rank astral entities. Rewards include a True Light, Summoner's Die: Form and an Immortal Crest.
128.name: Era Guide: The Reaper Trials (Book 2)

129.content: Single-use stones that awaken an essence ability, found, traded and rewarded by rank and rarity. What they do: "An awakening stone that unlocks the power of consumption... Effect: Awakens an essence ability", requiring an unawakened essence ability. The stone melts into the user's hand "with little fanfare". Why they matter: Rufus tells Jason he cannot "properly progress towards bronze rank until you awaken every essence ability you have. That's all twenty". Naming and rarity: stones are "unranked" and carry a rarity, such as the Awakening Stone of the Feast, of Adventure, of the Stars and of the Reaper. Affinity: the Reaper stone "sharing affinity with the Reaper" is used in Jason's awakening ritual with the Reaper token, and it gives Humphrey, a human, a special attack. Divine awakening stones: a god-made stone is "transcendent rank, epic" and bestows a specific aura power. Sources: looting an awakening stone or essence can pay better than the contract to kill the monster; the Adventure Society gives stones for exceptional service, "although rarely", and some open contracts offer them as rewards; otherwise stones are bought through brokers, almost always at auction, at exorbitant prices. Brokers in a small city hold the valuable stuff, like essences and stones, for big auctions. Family supply: the Gellers traditionally supply their scions with enough stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
129.name: Awakening Stones

130.content: The badge as an object: how an Adventure Society badge is made, tied to its wearer, tracked, altered and replaced, and what a guild membership adds on top. The organisation file explains what the Society does with badges; this file is about the item and the ways it fails. Who makes it: the Adventure Society manages the badges but the Magic Society creates them, taking an aura imprint from the new member inside a magic circle in about a minute. What it carries: every badge is paired with a tracking stone that tells the Society whether the member is alive or dead and finds them if they go missing. Members claim adventure notices with it and hold it against a security screen to close a contract. The wallet: the badge is a circular iron medallion embossed with a sword and rod crossed over a shield, carried in a leather wallet. Stars are on the metal: an official taps a wedge-shaped stone to the badge and a star is added, or removed. It tracks the badge, not the person: the tracking stones trace the badges, so a discarded badge hides its owner. A change of aura leaves the imprint on the badge unmatched, so the wearer cannot be tracked until a new badge is issued. When the Society wanted people's auras re-examined, their badges were also to be replaced. Jason's case: the stone cannot track his aura imprint, and Farrah says some people have abilities that block magical tracking.
130.name: Badges and Guild Membership

131.content: Emir's cloud ship and palace, and Jason's own cloud houses, yachts and palaces made from his Cloud Flask. Emir's cloud ship: it arrives at the Greenstone dock and a walkway of cloud connects to the shore as a hole opens in its side. Moored, it morphs over about ten minutes into a palace of clouds floating on the water. Emir's cloud palace: floating just offshore on the north side of the Island, "fully exposed to the waves and currents, yet remained as immovable as solid ground", with wings and towers in blue, purple, orange and gold. Walls, floors and ceilings glow with absorbed sunlight the palace stores and distributes, and the floors have a bouncy-castle spring. Low-magic limits: out of Greenstone the ship's full functionality is restored when Emir's cloud ship floats above Kurdansk. Team base: Jason's team move into Emir's palace after the contest. Jason's Cloud Flask: it creates buildings and vehicles of cloud, with forms limited by rank, iron cloud houses, bronze cloud vehicles and silver cloud palaces; items inside a returned construct are stored in a dimensional space until another is formed. Asano Village: Farrah prepares a place for Jason's cloud house at the end of a glass tunnel along the seafloor, two kilometres out, reached by a tramway from the compound and sealed by a wall of water, so the house can run underwater; the text checked does not show the house later sitting there.
131.name: Cloud Constructs and Cloud Palaces

132.comment: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
132.content: Single-use and crafting items: the City of Fallen Echoes rewards, clockwork cores, reality cores and star seeds. Lesser Miracle Potion: "iron rank, legendary", "Salvation in a bottle", it fully restores health, mana and stamina but only works on normal and iron-rank people, and its lingering magic delays other recovery. Medallion of Escape: "silver rank, uncommon", evacuates the holder from the astral space when their aura is projected into it, and only works inside the City of Fallen Echoes. Immortal Crest: "iron rank, rare", lets a mystical tattooist draw out a soul crest and only works on an iron-rank essence user. Summoner's Die: Form: "iron rank [growth], legendary", it randomly alters the form of an iron-rank summon. Clockwork Core: "iron rank, rare", the core of an artificial monster that simplifies the materials and processes of a construct creature; clockwork cores are made by clockwork kings. Star seeds: great astral beings, not gods, "can send their followers star seeds"; once implanted and germinated the body transforms, "minor or major". Reality cores: roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg, dark crystal glowing with transcendent light; one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it.

key: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
133.comment: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
133.content: The vehicles that cross the desert around Greenstone: the sand skimmers and sand barges Emir Bahadir's people run, the carriages that move expeditions to relay stations, and the monstrous Ustei war barge. Emir's cloud ship is covered in Cloud_Constructs_and_Palaces.md. Sand skimmers: small desert vehicles that carry a party across the sand. Emir leaves skimmers waiting at Boko to carry the team into the desert. Pushed past their limits: one of Emir's people specialises in magical tools and can periodically push the skimmers to speeds beyond their normal capability, so the whole vehicle vibrates. Their limits: skimmers cannot go through an astral-space aperture, so the party continues on foot. Requisitioned skimmers: expeditions requisition extra skimmers from the city and return them afterwards. Sand barges: larger vessels that move people and supplies overland. After Emir's ship sails south down the coast and into shore at an unremarkable patch of desert, his people unload three sand barges that carry the whole group inland to Sky Scar Lake. The trip takes hours more, into the night. Expedition transport: an expedition leaving Greenstone uses carriages to reach desert relay stations, then the captured Ustei barge and smaller barges supplied by the Magic Society.
keys: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
133.name: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges

134.content: How things and people are carried across a world without carts or roads: storage spaces that hold a person's goods, dimensional bags that expand them, and portal abilities that move people between places they have seen. Jason's own inventory and shadow gates are the best-documented examples, and the rest of the world treats both as everyday professional tools with hard limits. Jason's inventory is "a video-game inventory only Jason could see", unlike Clive's storage, which is opened by making a circle of floating runes with a portal inside. Dimensional bags are items with a rank. They add slots to an inventory in proportion to their rank, and at iron rank one bag slot is available and holds only iron-rank bags. Bags come in novelty shapes, such as a pair of boots. Storage as a profession: adventurers carry their possessions in dimensional bags or dimensional space abilities and travel light. Some portal workers "aren't even adventurers and do storage space transport for a living". Loot goes straight in: looted coins appear in the storage abilities of Clive, Humphrey and Jason, and Jason keeps a ledger of how much belongs to whom. Storage can be looted: Jason could have taken the items from Farrah's storage space by looting her body like a monster, and neither man suggested such a defilement. Limits on contents: it is "almost impossible to place living material inside dimensional storage", with only a few carefully chosen plants viable.
134.name: Dimensional Storage and Portals

135.content: Jason's combat robes are the flowing, tailored armour that gives him his dark, shadowy look. The first is the Trap Weaver Battle Robe, bought from Gilbert Bertinelli in Book 1; it is replaced at each rank by a new robe made by Gilbert from monster materials Jason supplies. The robes are armour in a robe's cut, stored in his inventory and swapped on by the outfits tab.
135.name: Jason's Combat Robes

key: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
136.comment: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
136.content: ; Dread Salvation: a sword "crafted with gratitude, in hope it would be of the greatest use in the moment of greatest need"; "iron rank [growth], legendary"; when an affliction special attack meets a physical immunity it gains Stone Cutter, and for a magical immunity Spell Breaker. Gary made it, as a gift. The window says it "must be reforged by the original craftsperson in order to advance further". Cloud Flask: iron rank growth item that Jason binds in Book 2; it creates cloud buildings and vehicles, with forms limited by rank. Its maker is "some unknown diamond-rank craftsman". Amulet of the Dark Guardian: silver rank growth item, the last item produced by his old quest system, a reproduction of his personal crest on an obsidian chain. Its boon Guardian's Blessing absorbs damage per affliction applied and can be given to another person by touch. Regalia of the Dark Hegemon: the set bonuses are Hegemon's Authority from the amulet (allies in his aura resist aura suppression, and he can spend instances to strengthen his own suppression), a mist shroud from the cloud flask, and mana drain with Hegemon's Tribute from the sword. Robes of the Astral Verdict: bronze rank, rare cloth armour for summoners that boosts dimension spells, summon damage reduction and disruptive-force resistance.
